title: Song of Solomon 4
paragraphs: ¹ How beautiful you are, my love! How beautiful! Your eyes are doves behind your veil. Your hair is like a flock of goats streaming down from the hills of Gilead. ² Your teeth are like a flock of newly shorn sheep just come up from washing — each one perfectly paired, not one missing. ³ Your lips are like a scarlet thread, and your mouth is lovely. Your cheeks behind your veil are like the halves of a pomegranate. ⁴ Your neck is like the tower of David, built in courses of stone; a thousand shields hang upon it, all the armor of warriors. ⁵ Your two breasts are like two young fawns, twins of a gazelle, feeding among the lilies.

⁶ Until the day breaks and the shadows flee away, I will go to the mountain of myrrh and the hill of frankincense. ⁷ You are altogether beautiful, my love; there is no flaw in you. ⁸ Come with me from Lebanon, my bride; come with me from Lebanon. Descend from the peak of Amana, from the summit of Senir and Hermon — from the lions' dens and the leopard-haunted hills. ⁹ You have captured my heart, my sister, my bride! You have stolen my heart with one glance of your eyes, with one jewel of your necklace. ¹⁰ How beautiful is your love, my sister, my bride! How much sweeter your love than wine, and the fragrance of your perfumes than any spice!

¹¹ Your lips, my bride, drip with honey; milk and honey are under your tongue. The fragrance of your garments is like the fragrance of Lebanon. ¹² My sister, my bride, is a garden enclosed — a spring shut up, a fountain sealed. ¹³ Your branches are an orchard of pomegranates bearing precious fruit — henna blossoms and nard, ¹⁴ nard and saffron, calamus and cinnamon, with every kind of incense tree; myrrh and aloes with all the finest spices. ¹⁵ You are a garden fountain, a well of living water, flowing streams from Lebanon.
¹⁶ "Awake, north wind! Come, south wind! Blow upon my garden and let its fragrance pour forth. Let my beloved come into his garden and taste its choicest fruits."
